Now I shall fully explain another supreme sādhana of Vārāhī. By means of the yoga of the generation stage (utpattikrama), one should visualize one's own body as resembling twelve suns and like the powder of vermilion.
[She is] blue, with a lotus as her seat, having three faces and six arms;
she is fully adorned with all ornaments, well-seated in the sattva-paryaṅka posture, wearing a crown of garlands of skulls, with disheveled hair, and auspicious. [125]
She is in union with Vajraghaṇṭā, her breasts pressed by his skillful means;
she holds an arrow and a gaṇḍī-bell, her ears filled and agitated;
she carries a skull-cup and a khaṭvāṅga staff, intent on drawing [beings] in with a hook.
She who dwells in the center of a red lotus, the bestower of all desires.
Alternatively, [one may visualize her] with twelve arms and six faces, born of a divine body,
with an upward-facing face and a boar’s head, possessing divine splendor and fierce majesty; she is Vajraguhyottamā on the eastern petal.
In the north is Vajrasamayottamā; in the west, Vajratejottamā;
in the south, Vajraratnottamā.
In the southeast is Vajrajñānottamā; in the southwest is Vajravidyottamā;
and in the northwest is Vajrasiddhottamā.
In the northeast is Vajrabhasmottamā;
at the gates are Vajrajvālottamā, Vajrāmṛtottamā, Vajrakrodhottamā, and Vajradraṣṭottamā.
These goddesses are red in color, with three faces, six arms, and three eyes; they stand in the sattva-paryaṅka posture, with loose hair and adorned with all ornaments.

Absorbed in union with the Vajra-bell, joined with her own body as the means (upāya), she holds a noose, a hook, a skull-cup, and a khaṭvāṅga; four such figures are stationed in the corners holding a bow and arrow. At the gates, she stands in the ālīḍha posture, naked, with a distorted face.
All the preta-seated [deities] hold a noose joined with the vajra-rolling gesture (vajrollālana) and the threatening forefinger;
in others, they are as in one another;
according to the sequence, they possess the emblems in the assembly.
Having visualized that [deity] together with body, speech, and mind within the heart of the Wisdom Goddess,
one should become of equal flavor (*samarasa*) with all phenomena through the yoga of the wisdom-maṇḍala.
One should cause [the deity] to emanate through the recitation of wisdom and, according to the procedure of withdrawal, [dissolve it] gradually.
And through the recitation of the supreme samaya, the reality of mantra is accomplished.
Oṃ śrīvajravārāhī āḥ baṃ hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ śrīvajraguhyottame hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ śrīvajrasamayottame hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ śrīvajratejottame hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ śrīvajraratnottame hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā |
Oṃ śrīvajrajñānottame hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ śrīvajravidyottame hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā.
Oṃ śrīvajrajvālottame hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā |
Oṃ śrīvajrāmṛtottame hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ śrīvajrakrodhottame hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ śrīvajradraṣṭrottame hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā ||
Thus, one should perform the meditation on recitation in the proper sequence.
For the nature of all phenomena is indeed the reality (dharmatā) characterized by the process of withdrawal and emanation.
One who is the self of the yoga with one’s own chosen deity should visualize all sentient beings as such.
One should cause the phenomena of the stations of yoga to enter into the three secrets;
the phenomena of the abode of the three secrets are like the suchness of the nature of phenomena.
Regarding the phenomena of the selflessness of phenomena, there are neither phenomena nor a nature of phenomena.
In the *Abhidhānottarottara*, this is the thirty-third chapter, the glorious *Guhyasamayottama*.

[1262'] The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara beheld those five hundred maidens and said to them: "Daughters of good family, do not fear; I shall deliver you from this great mass of suffering. Then, having comforted those five hundred maidens, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara proceeded toward the place where the Blessed One was staying. Having arrived there, he prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, while I was traveling along the highway, I heard the cries of weeping and lamentation from a great distance. Upon investigation, I saw five hundred maidens bound with five hundred cords, their heads shorn, their hair disheveled, and their faces covered with dust. They were being led away by a caravan of merchants to be sold into slavery. Seeing them thus, I approached and asked: 'Daughters of good family, why are you crying out in such distress? They replied: 'Noble sir, we have been seized by robbers and are being led away to be sold into slavery. Thereupon, I spoke to them: 'Daughters of good family, do not fear; I shall deliver you from this great mass of suffering. [1263] The Blessed One then said to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara: "Excellent, excellent, son of good family! It is wonderful that you possess such great compassion for sentient beings. Son of good family, it is because you have cultivated the roots of virtue over many hundreds of thousands of millions of eons that you now manifest such great compassion for sentient beings. [1264] The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara then addressed the Blessed One: "Blessed One, if a man or woman were to hear the name of me, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, they would be freed from all fear. Blessed One, if anyone were to be bound in shackles, fetters, or stocks, and were to call upon my name, the bonds would be loosened and they would be released. Blessed One, if anyone were to be threatened by fire, water, poison, or weapons, and were to call upon my name, they would be delivered from that danger. Blessed One, if anyone were to travel along a perilous path infested with robbers and bandits, and were to call upon my name, they would safely reach their destination. [1265] The Blessed One then said to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara: "Son of good family, it is so; it is exactly as you say. If anyone hears your name, they will be freed from all fear.
